axes.model_access: The root of the GGUF ecosystem: the official server runs F16 and quantised models on GPU/CPU, with models taken from Hugging Face as GGUF or converted from safetensors; supported model families roll with merges, while quantised files come from community quantisers (2026-11-21).
axes.runtime: A C/C++ inference library plus `llama-server`: OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, embeddings and responses, and an Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages`. Build backends cover CPU, Metal, SYCL, CUDA, HIP and Vulkan, with a built-in web UI (2026-11-21).
axes.local_files: Fully local: model weights, KV cache, conversations and outputs stay on the user’s machine; `--kv-offload` moves KV cache to GPU while `--no-kv-offload` keeps it on CPU, and there is no official cloud-hosted line (2026-11-21).
axes.background: `llama-server` is a long-running service: continuous batching is on by default, `-np/--parallel` sets slot count and `--ctx-checkpoints` retains context checkpoints. It suits an always-on process, with any hosted queue built by the deployer (2026-11-21).
axes.tools: A strong tool surface: `--jinja` enables OpenAI-style function calling/tool use with native formats plus a generic fallback for any model; experimental `--mcp-servers-json` connects Cursor-compatible MCP servers; `--agent` enables built-in tools and a CORS proxy; plus schema-constrained JSON, multimodal, reranking and monitoring endpoints (2026-11-21).
axes.context: Context is controlled at launch: `-c/--ctx-size` sets the prompt window, `--kv-unified-per-slot` caps each parallel slot, `-ctk/-ctv` compress KV cache to q8/q4 types and `--ctx-checkpoints` retains up to 32 checkpoints (2026-11-21).
axes.permissions: MIT licensed with no account system for the local process; `llama-server` authenticates Bearer keys via `--api-key` or `--api-key-file`; MCP/agent are off by default and, when enabled, restrict CORS to localhost for safety, with official warnings against untrusted environments (2026-11-21).
axes.fit: Fit: fine-grained control over quantisation, backends, context and KV cache; GGUF on consumer hardware; a local inference base for downstream tools; MCP/tool calling at the server layer. Not fit: turnkey GUIs or high-throughput multi-model serving (vLLM/SGLang are stronger there) (2026-11-21).

runs: This entry checks the official server, function-calling and build docs plus the repo licence. Throughput, VRAM and MCP tool-chain stability need testing on specific hardware and models.
